Ares / Artemis Outpost: Survival & Balance Ares / Artemis Outpost: Survival & Balance is a web-based planetary engineering simulator and STEM educational platform developed in the "Altyn Tüyün" Laboratory of the Naryn branch of NDITA for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. The project places players in the role of Mission Commander overseeing the establishment and long-term viability of human habitats on the Moon (Artemis Base Alpha) and Mars (Ares Outpost Prime). details:
Project Overview: Ares / Artemis Outpost: Survival & Balance

Developed by: "Altyn Tüyün" Laboratory, Naryn Branch of the National Children's Engineering and Technical Academy (NDITA)
Event: NASA Space Apps Challenge
Platform: Web Application (Cross-platform, Responsive)

1. What It Does and How It Works

Ares / Artemis Outpost: Survival & Balance is an interactive planetary engineering simulator and STEM educational platform. It immerses players into the role of Mission Commander responsible for the establishment, daily survival, and technological progression of humanity's initial permanent colonies: Artemis Base Alpha (on the Moon) and Ares Outpost Prime (on Mars).

Core Mechanics & Workflow:

  • Resource & Telemetry Management: The simulation runs over a 30-Sol expedition. Each day (Sol), players monitor six interrelated life support metrics: Energy (kWh), Oxygen (O2O_2O2​), Water (H2OH_2OH2​O), Food rations, Cosmic Radiation exposure (mSv), and Crew Health (%).
    1. ECLSS (Environmental Control and Life Support System): Governs oxygen replenishment via water electrolysis and CO2CO_2CO2​ scrubbers.
    2. Hydroponic Agrodome: Produces fresh biomass and food rations through automated LED photosynthetic cycles.
    3. Electromagnetic Radiation Deflector: Deflects incoming solar proton events (SPE) and deep-space galactic cosmic rays (GCR). Underpowering any system triggers immediate cascading degradation (e.g., hypoxia, crop wilting, or radiation sickness).
  • Authentic Aerospace Dilemmas: Every Sol introduces random mission events based on real-world spaceflight risks—such as regolith seal micro-cracks, dust storm solar occlusion (τ≥2.5\tau \ge 2.5τ≥2.5), telemetry telemetry desynchronization, and thermal pump cavitation. Players must evaluate risk trade-offs, balancing crew safety against dwindling reserves.
  • Research & Technology Tree: Science points earned by surviving crises can be reinvested into advanced NASA-derived technologies, such as closed-loop water catalytic distillation, aeroponic vertical farming, graphene composite hull reinforcement, and AI predictive maintenance.
    • An authentic 3D model of the Solar System with accurate orbital kinematics, planetary scales, atmospheres, and NASA fact sheets.
    • 3D representations of human orbital habitats (ISS, Lunar Gateway) and milestone exploration missions (James Webb Space Telescope, Perseverance Rover).
    • Comprehensive 15-question examinations with dynamically shuffled questions and answer options, culminating in an official Mission Commander Certificate.

2. Benefits of the Project

  • Transforms Abstract Equations into Intuitive Experience: Rather than presenting aerospace engineering as passive textbook formulas, the simulator visualizes the direct cause-and-effect relationships of life support thermodynamics, the Sabatier reaction, and radiation shielding.
  • Zero-Barrier Accessibility: Runs entirely in modern web browsers without requiring installations, account registrations, high-end GPUs, or proprietary plugins.
  • Dual Value (Gaming + Education): Functions simultaneously as an engaging strategy survival game for enthusiasts and a rigorous pedagogical tool for classrooms, youth clubs, and science centers.
  • Promotes Critical Thinking and Risk Assessment: Encourages players to think like NASA flight controllers—anticipating bottlenecks, maintaining safety margins, and planning for worst-case scenarios.

3. Expected Impact

  • Inspiring Regional and Global Youth in STEM: Initiated in the mountain region of Naryn, Kyrgyzstan, through the "Altyn Tüyün" academy, the project demonstrates that young learners in emerging technology communities can design world-class aerospace software and contribute meaningfully to global space challenges.
  • Advancing NASA Open Science: The project brings official NASA scientific datasets (Planetary Fact Sheets, Curiosity RAD, Perseverance MOXIE, ISS ECLSS) directly to public awareness in an interactive, easy-to-digest medium.
  • Scalable Educational Deployment: Because of its lightweight, web-native architecture, schools and STEM hubs worldwide can integrate the simulator into physics, astronomy, and computer science curricula at zero cost.

4. Tools, Programming Languages, Hardware, and Software Used

  • Programming Languages:
    • JavaScript (Modern ES6+ / JSX): Core application architecture, simulation engine, and state management.
    • HTML5 & CSS3: Semantic markup, canvas rendering, and responsive spatial layout.
    • React 18: Component-driven user interface, reactive hooks, and modular UI state synchronization.
    • Three.js (WebGL): 3D graphics rendering engine used for the orbital launch intro, interactive Solar System, and space station models.
    • Tailwind CSS: Modern utility-first styling delivering an authentic retro-futuristic NASA Mission Control visual identity.
    • Web Audio API: Custom procedural sound synthesis engine providing dynamic telemetry beeps, emergency klaxons, and atmospheric ambient cues without relying on heavy external audio files.
    • Vite: High-performance local development server and optimized rollup production bundler.
    • Node.js: Automated balance verification test suites (running 100-run Monte Carlo stress tests for game fairness).
    • Git & Terminal (macOS/Unix): Version control, branch hygiene, and build pipelines.

5. Creativity of the Project

  • Narrative Launch Sequence from Naryn to Orbit: The project features a cinematic 3D prologue visualizing an "Altyn Tüyün" communications satellite launching directly from the high-altitude valley of Naryn, ascending through the stratosphere, docking with an orbital space station, and transitioning seamlessly into mission control. This bridges local cultural identity with international space exploration.
  • Procedural NASA Mission Control Aesthetic: The interface mirrors authentic telemetry consoles, combining phosphor-green and cyan displays, dynamic graphs, warning indicators, and procedural audio cues that deliver an authentic, high-stakes aerospace atmosphere.
  • Dynamic, Anti-Rote Exam Engine: Unlike static online quizzes where answers can be memorized by position, our quiz system executes a Fisher-Yates runtime shuffle for both question sequence and choices (A, B, C, D), requiring authentic conceptual understanding to earn certification.
  • Synthetic 2D/3D Hybrid Visualization: Blends crisp 2D isometric base representations with rich real-time 3D planetary and orbital models, ensuring fluid 60 FPS performance even on budget laptops or classroom tablets.

6. Key Factors Considered by Our Team

  1. Scientific Authenticity vs. Playability: We rigorously grounded all numbers in real NASA data (0.84 kg O2O_2O2​/day, 2.5 L H2OH_2OH2​O/day, 0.25 mSv/day radiation baseline), while tuning consumable burn rates so that players experience realistic operational pressure within a manageable 30-Sol gaming session.
  2. Deterministic Simulation Engine: We decoupled the core mathematical engine (SimulationEngine.js) from the visual UI layer. This enabled us to run automated 100-iteration Monte Carlo balance tests ensuring that careless play always fails while sound scientific planning consistently succeeds.
  3. Hardware Independence & Performance: Understanding that classrooms may use diverse or low-power hardware, we avoided heavy 3D textures. Instead, we utilized procedural geometry, canvas text sprites, and lightweight shaders to keep memory usage minimal and load times under 2 seconds.
  4. Inclusive Bilingual Documentation: We ensured that the project's documentation, scientific references, and background data are accessible in both English and Russian, facilitating local regional mentorship and international competition review.
  5. Resilience and Offline Readiness: The production package is fully standalone with relative resource paths, enabling local execution even in remote educational centers with limited or intermittent internet connectivity.
